The shipped example shows the\n14\tshape of the problem: `example/weather-tool.ts` declares `location` as a required string, then\n15\tcasts and defaults it (`(input.location as string) || 'Unknown'`) with a comment warning the reader\n16\tthat `inputSchema` shapes what the model sends but does not enforce it. That is the careful version,\n17\twritten by the people who wrote the engine — and it still answers a malformed call with a\n18\tconfidently formatted forecast for `'Unknown'` rather than telling the model it got the call wrong.\n19\t\n20\tThe registry currently pushes this check onto each tool's own executor, leaving every consumer\n21\tto implement it itself — differently each time, or not at all. Validation enforces `required`, declared types and `enum` only —\n41\tit does not inject `additionalProperties: false`, coerce types, or apply defaults, and\n42\tthere is no opt-out flag.\n43\t\n44\tUpdate `docs/adding-a-tool.md`, `README.md` and `.specify/spec.md` to match.\n45\t\n46\t## Acceptance criteria\n47\t\n48\t- [ ] `ToolRegistry.execute` validates `input` against the resolved definition's\n49\t      `inputSchema` before calling the executor; The shipped example shows the\nshape of the problem: `example/weather-tool.ts` declares `location` as a required string, then\ncasts and defaults it (`(input.location as string) || 'Unknown'`) with a comment warning the reader\nthat `inputSchema` shapes what the model sends but does not enforce it. properties: {location: {type: 'string'}},\n          required: ['location'],\n        },\n      },\n      async () => {\n        executorCalls += 1;\n        return 'sunny';\n      }\n    );\n\n 'ssn_lookup',\n        description: 'Look up record by identifier',\n        inputSchema: {\n          type: 'object',\n          properties: {ssn: {type: 'string'}},\n          required: ['ssn'],\n        },\n      },\n      async () => {\n        executorCalls += 1;\n        return 'found';\n      }\n    );\n\n    const response = await registry.execute('ssn_lookup', {ssn: 123456789});\n\n    expect({\n      executorCalls,\n      mentionsField: response.result.includes('ssn'),\n      mentionsExpectedType: response.result.includes('string'),\n      leaksValueInResult: response.result.includes('123456789'),\n      leaksValueInLogs: recordedLogs.some(line => line.includes('123456789')),\n    }).toEqual({\n      executorCalls: 0,\n      mentionsField: true,\n      mentionsExpectedType: true,\n      leaksValueInResult: false,\n      leaksValueInLogs: false,\n    });\n  });\n\n  it('throws at register time naming the tool when a static inputSchema cannot be description: 'Get weather for a location',\n        inputSchema: {\n          type: 'object',\n          properties: {location: {type: 'string'}},\n          required: ['location'],\n        },\n      }),\n      async input => {\n        executorInputs.push(input);\n        return `22C in ${String(input.location)}`;\n      }\n    );\n\n    let firstRoundToolResult = '';\n    let round = 0;\n    const provider: AIProvider = {\n      async *sendMessage(params: SendMessageParams): AsyncGenerator<MessageChunk> {\n        round += 1;\n        if (round === 1) {\n          yield {type: 'tool_use', statement.body.length : 1;\n}\n/** Unwrapping an else block hoists its statements into the enclosing scope; a\n *  top-level declaration there could collide, so those keep a human's eyes. */\nfunction declaresBindings(alternate) {\n    if (alternate.type !== \"BlockStatement\") {\n        return DECLARATIONS.has(alternate.type);\n    }\n    return alternate.body.some((statement) => DECLARATIONS.has(statement.type));\n}\nfunction fixUnnecessaryElse(sourceCode, fixer, node) {\n    const elseToken = sourceCode.getTokenBefore(node.alternate, (token) => token.type === \"Keyword\" && token.value === \"else\");\n    // `else if (...)` — dropping the keyword leaves a sibling if.\n    if (node.alternate.type === \"IfStatement\") {\n        return fixer.removeRange([elseToken.range[0], node.alternate.range[0]]);\n    }\n    // `else { ... }` — replace keyword-through-block with the block's body.\n    if (node.alternate.type === \"BlockStatement\") {\n        const inner = sourceCode.getText(node.alternate).slice(1, -1).trim();\n        return fixer.replaceTextRange([elseToken.range[0], node.alternate.range[1]], inner);\n    }\n    // `else statement;` — just drop the keyword.\n    return fixer.removeRange([elseToken.range[0], node.alternate.range[0]]);\n}\n/** Shape 1: the report for an if that carries an else. */\nfunction elseDescriptor(sourceCode, node) {\n    if (!terminates(node.consequent)) {\n        return { node, messageId: \"splitIntoTwoIfs\" };\n    }\n    const fixable = !declaresBindings(node.alternate);\n    return {\n        node: node.alternate,\n        messageId: \"unnecessaryElse\",\n        data: { how: \"returns\" },\n        fix: fixable\n            ? {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"call_769f459dce304aa58306514f","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t# Tool Input Validation\n2\t\n3\t| Field  | Value                |\n4\t| ------ | -------------------- |\n5\t| Issue  | re-cinq/HALEngine#37 |\n6\t| Status | In Progress          |\n7\t\n8\tEvery tool registered in `src/orchestration/tools/registry.ts` declares a JSON Schema `inputSchema` that is forwarded to the configured AI provider, and `ToolRegistry.execute` validates the model-supplied `input` against that schema before calling the tool's executor. When validation fails, `execute` returns a rejection `ToolResponse` describing what was wrong rather than throwing, so the orchestrator feeds the failure back to the model as a `tool_result` within the existing tool-round budget.\n9\t\n10\t## Validation at execute time\n11\t\n12\t- When `input` omits a property listed in `required`, `ToolRegistry.execute` returns a `ToolResponse` whose `result` names the missing property as required and never invokes the executor ([validated by: rejects input missing a required property with a ToolResponse and never calls the executor](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.acceptance.test.ts#L16)).\n13\t- When `input` supplies a property whose value does not match its declared JSON Schema type, `ToolRegistry.execute` returns a `ToolResponse` naming the failing field path and expected type without invoking the executor, and neither `result` nor the emitted log record contains the offending property value ([validated by: rejects a wrong-typed property naming the field and expected type without leaking the offending value to the result or logs](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.acceptance.test.ts#L46)).\n14\t- When `input` satisfies `required`, declared property types and `enum`, `ToolRegistry.execute` invokes the executor once and passes the input object through unchanged — including undeclared extra properties — without injecting `additionalProperties: false`, coercing types or applying defaults.\n15\t- When `ToolRegistry.execute` is called with a tool name that has not been registered, it throws `Unknown tool: <name>` because an unregistered tool is a programming or configuration error rather than a recoverable input mistake.\n16\t\n17\t## Schema compilation and caching\n18\t\n19\t- A static `ToolDefinition` has its `inputSchema` compiled once at `register` time, so a schema that is not valid JSON Schema throws synchronously from `register` with an error message naming the offending tool ([validated by: throws at register time naming the tool when a static inputSchema cannot be compiled](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.acceptance.test.ts#L94), [validated by: throws at registration time naming the tool for an uncompilable schema](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.test.ts#L4)).\n20\t- A static tool's `inputSchema` is compiled at `register` time and reused on every `execute` call without re-reading or re-compiling `definition.inputSchema`.\n21\t- A function-valued `ToolDefinitionSource` resolves its definition on each `execute` call and validates against the `inputSchema` returned for that call, caching compiled validators by schema object reference (`WeakMap`) so distinct returned schemas each enforce their own rules.\n22\t\n23\t## Orchestrator tool-loop recovery\n24\t\n25\t- Because a schema rejection returns a `ToolResponse` instead of throwing, `src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.ts` sends the rejection `result` back to the provider as a `tool_result` message, allowing the model to issue a corrected tool call on the next round and complete the turn within `maxToolRounds` ([validated by: returns a schema rejection as a tool_result in the orchestrator loop so the model can correct the call on the next round](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.acceptance.test.ts#L112)).\n26\t"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"ee11d90f-fc8e-4737-93f5-aee635892159","uuid":"6303a862-c269-46a4-88ff-f28184774041","timestamp":"2026-11-03T11:06:04.357Z","tool_use_result":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"/var/tmp/loop-bench/runs/ed7c55279f96/workspace/target/specs/hal-engine-tool-input-validation/spec.md","content":"# Tool Input Validation\n\n| Field  | Value                |\n| ------ | -------------------- |\n| Issue  | re-cinq/HALEngine#37 |\n| Status | In Progress          |\n\nEvery tool registered in `src/orchestration/tools/registry.ts` declares a JSON Schema `inputSchema` that is forwarded to the configured AI provider, and `ToolRegistry.execute` validates the model-supplied `input` against that schema before calling the tool's executor. When validation fails, `execute` returns a rejection `ToolResponse` describing what was wrong rather than throwing, so the orchestrator feeds the failure back to the model as a `tool_result` within the existing tool-round budget.\n\n## Validation at execute time\n\n- When `input` omits a property listed in `required`, `ToolRegistry.execute` returns a `ToolResponse` whose `result` names the missing property as required and never invokes the executor ([validated by: rejects input missing a required property with a ToolResponse and never calls the executor](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.acceptance.test.ts#L16)).\n- When `input` supplies a property whose value does not match its declared JSON Schema type, `ToolRegistry.execute` returns a `ToolResponse` naming the failing field path and expected type without invoking the executor, and neither `result` nor the emitted log record contains the offending property value ([validated by: rejects a wrong-typed property naming the field and expected type without leaking the offending value to the result or logs](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.acceptance.test.ts#L46)).\n- When `input` satisfies `required`, declared property types and `enum`, `ToolRegistry.execute` invokes the executor once and passes the input object through unchanged — including undeclared extra properties — without injecting `additionalProperties: false`, coercing types or applying defaults.\n- When `ToolRegistry.execute` is called with a tool name that has not been registered, it throws `Unknown tool: <name>` because an unregistered tool is a programming or configuration error rather than a recoverable input mistake.\n\n## Schema compilation and caching\n\n- A static `ToolDefinition` has its `inputSchema` compiled once at `register` time, so a schema that is not valid JSON Schema throws synchronously from `register` with an error message naming the offending tool ([validated by: throws at register time naming the tool when a static inputSchema cannot be compiled](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.acceptance.test.ts#L94), [validated by: throws at registration time naming the tool for an uncompilable schema](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.test.ts#L4)).\n- A static tool's `inputSchema` is compiled at `register` time and reused on every `execute` call without re-reading or re-compiling `definition.inputSchema`.\n- A function-valued `ToolDefinitionSource` resolves its definition on each `execute` call and validates against the `inputSchema` returned for that call, caching compiled validators by schema object reference (`WeakMap`) so distinct returned schemas each enforce their own rules.\n\n## Orchestrator tool-loop recovery\n\n- Because a schema rejection returns a `ToolResponse` instead of throwing, `src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.ts` sends the rejection `result` back to the provider as a `tool_result` message, allowing the model to issue a corrected tool call on the next round and complete the turn within `maxToolRounds` ([validated by: returns a schema rejection as a tool_result in the orchestrator loop so the model can correct the call on the next round](../../src/orchestration/tools/registry.acceptance.test.ts#L112)).\n","numLines":26,"startLine":1,"totalLines":26}},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"call_769f459dce304aa58306514f","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}

{"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"call_57092551d43e4a6f841c13d9","type":"tool_result","content":"# Changelog\n\nAll notable changes to `@re-cinq/hal-engine` are documented here.\n\nThe format is [Keep a Changelog 1.1.0](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/), and this project adheres to\n[Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html). Entries are written for somebody installing the\npackage, not for somebody reading this repository's commit log.\n\n## [Unreleased]\n\n### Changed\n\n- **Breaking:** `ToolRegistry.register` now compiles a tool's `inputSchema` with `ajv` (`strict: false`, `validateFormats: false`) at registration time and throws naming the tool when the schema is not valid JSON Schema.\n\n## [0.3.0] - 2026-09-17\n\n### Changed\n\n- `HalEngineConfig.orchestrator.hooks` now carries a JSDoc comment. The field already shipped\n  in `0.2.x`; the comment makes the lifecycle-hook seam discoverable from the published type\n  declarations so editors surface it on hover without a trip to the README.\n\n## [0.2.1] - 2026-09-14\n\nIdentical to `0.2.0` — same files, same code. It exists to prove that a release publishes with no\ncredential stored in the repository: `0.2.0` had to be published with a token, because the registry\ncannot hold a trusted publisher for a name that has never been published, and this is the first version\nreleased through that publisher instead. There is nothing here to upgrade for.\n\n## [0.2.0] - 2026-09-14\n\nThe first release under the `@re-cinq` scope. Nothing has been published before it, so there is no upgrade\npath from `0.1.0` on the registry — only from the git specifier.\n\n### Changed\n\n- The published package carries no source maps. `files` is `[\"dist\"]`, so every `.js.map` and `.d.ts.map`\n  named a `../src/*.ts` the tarball did not contain and carried no inlined sources — 98 files that resolved\n  to nothing in a debugger. Dropping them halves the file count. Step through the source from a checkout\n  of the repository instead.\n=== version:\n3:  \"version\": \"0.4.0\",\n=== changelog script:\n#!/usr/bin/env bash\n# Fails when a diff touches src/ and leaves CHANGELOG.md alone.\n#\n# Usage:\n#   bash scripts/check-changelog.sh [base-ref]     # default: origin/main\n#\n# The rule is about what a consumer can observe, not about effort: anything that\n# changes shipped behaviour needs a sentence they can read on npm. A change to\n# src/ that genuinely is not user-visible - an internal refactor, a test-only\n# edit - takes the `no-changelog` label instead, which is a deliberate, visible\n# act rather than a silent omission.\nset -uo pipefail\n\nbase=\"${1:-origin/main}\"\n\n# A base ref that does not resolve means nothing was compared. On a laptop that\n# is ordinary - a fresh clone has no origin/main - and skipping is right. In CI\n# it is the gate passing without running, which is the one outcome a gate must\n# never have, and it is exactly how a fetch that failed went unnoticed.\nif ! git rev-parse --verify --quiet \"$base\" >/dev/null; then\n  if [ -n \"${GITHUB_ACTIONS:-}\" ]; then\n    echo \"check-changelog: FAILED - base ref '$base' does not resolve, so nothing was checked\" >&2\n    exit 1\n  fi\n  echo \"check-changelog: base ref '$base' not found; skipping\" >&2\n  exit 0\nfi\n\nmerge_base=\"$(git merge-base \"$base\" HEAD)\"\nchanged=\"$(git diff --name-only \"$merge_base\"..HEAD)\"","is_error":false}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"ee11d90f-fc8e-4737-93f5-aee635892159","uuid":"1be37667-112f-4968-8043-80d252101b3c","timestamp":"2026-11-03T11:06:41.595Z","tool_use_result":{"stdout":"# Changelog\n\nAll notable changes to `@re-cinq/hal-engine` are documented here.\n\nThe format is [Keep a Changelog 1.1.0](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/), and this project adheres to\n[Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html). {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"call_071db0a75e0b4ce7b5297ce4","type":"tool_result","content":"/**\n * require-status-matches-coverage — a spec.md / ADR must declare the lifecycle\n * status its test links can support, and must declare one the parsers can read.\n *\n * Status is the org's backlog signal: the web-UI pills render it, spec-status-upkeep\n * flips it, humans trust it. This rule makes it answerable to the corpus's own\n * `([validated by](test.ts#Lnn))` links rather than to whoever last edited the row:\n *\n *   no testable statement linked    -> Draft\n *   some testable statements linked -> In Progress\n *   every testable statement linked -> Shipped\n *\n * The per-doc complement of `require-statement-links` (which nags per unlinked\n * statement); both read the same `statementCoverage` walk, so the two rules can\n * never disagree about what is linked. Skips `rejected` / `retired` docs via the\n * shared `statusTier`, and docs with no testable statements (no tier to infer).\n *\n * Which folders hold the corpus comes from the `roots` option\n * (`{ spec: [\"specs\"], adr: [\"adrs\"] }` by default) — see `lib/status-coverage.mjs`\n * for the coverage walk.\n *\n * Deliberately carries no `fix`/`suggest`: the `format` CI job runs\n * `eslint --fix` and commits the result back, so a fixer here would silently\n * rewrite spec statuses across the repo on every PR. The message names the label\n * to write; a human writes it.\n */\nimport { statusLabel } from \"./lib/spec-parsers.mjs\";\nimport { DOC_ROOTS_SCHEMA, docKind } from \"./lib/doc-kind.mjs\";\nimport { statusMismatch } from \"./lib/status-coverage.mjs\";\nconst CORPUS = { spec: \"spec\", adr: \"ADR\" };\nconst REQUIREMENT = {\n    spec: \"Add a `| Status | Draft |` row to the header table (one of Draft / In Progress / Shipped / Rejected / Retired).\",\n    adr: \"Add `status: draft` to the YAML frontmatter (one of draft / in progress / shipped / rejected / retired).\",\n};\nfunction mismatchReport(mismatch, kind) {\n    const loc = { line: mismatch.line, column: 1 };\n    if (mismatch.reason === \"untagged\") {\n        return {\n            loc,\n            messageId: \"untagged\",\n            data: { corpus: CORPUS[kind], requirement: REQUIREMENT[kind] },\n        };\n    }\n    return {\n        loc,\n        messageId: \"statusMismatch\",\n        data: {\n            corpus: CORPUS[kind],\n            actual: mismatch.actual,\n            expected: statusLabel(mismatch.expected, kind),\n            linked: mismatch.linked,\n            testable: mismatch.testable,\n        },\n    };\n}\nexport default {\n    meta: {\n        type: \"problem\",\n        docs: {\n            description: \"require every spec.md / ADR to declare a parseable lifecycle status that matches its test-link coverage: no links -> Draft, some -> In Progress, all -> Shipped. Skips rejected/retired docs and docs with no testable statements.\",\n        },\n        schema: [\n            {\n                type: \"object\",\n                properties: { roots: DOC_ROOTS_SCHEMA },\n                additionalProperties: false,\n            },\n        ],\n        messages: {\n            untagged: \"This {{corpus}} declares no status the parsers can read, so its coverage cannot be checked and no status can be rendered for it. {{requirement}}\",\n            statusMismatch: 'Status \"{{actual}}\" does not match this {{corpus}}\\'s test-link coverage — {{linked}} of {{testable}} testable statements carry a ([validated by](test.ts#Lline)) link. Either set the status to \"{{expected}}\", or link the remaining statements to the tests that validate them.',\n        },\n    },\n    create(context) {\n        const kind = docKind(context.filename, context.options[0]?.roots);\n        if (!kind) {\n            return {};\n        }\n        const text = context.sourceCode.getText();\n        return {\n            \"root:exit\"() {\n                const mismatch = statusMismatch(text, kind);\n                if (mismatch) {\n                    context.report(mismatchReport(mismatch, kind));\n                }\n            },\n        };\n    },\n};","is_error":false}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"ee11d90f-fc8e-4737-93f5-aee635892159","uuid":"d4c1f248-c64c-4e2b-81d1-e1f037ce5c02","timestamp":"2026-11-03T11:10:02.071Z","tool_use_result":{"stdout":"/**\n * require-status-matches-coverage — a spec.md / ADR must declare the lifecycle\n * status its test links can support, and must declare one the parsers can read.\n *\n * Status is the org's backlog signal: the web-UI pills render it, spec-status-upkeep\n * flips it, humans trust it. {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"call_371e12be29b246988e39a9d9","type":"tool_result","content":"110\tGuidelines:\n111\t- Write prompts as natural user questions, not technical descriptions\n112\t- Keep them short and specific -- they appear as pill-shaped buttons in the UI\n113\t- 1-2 prompts per tool is enough; the total across all tools should stay manageable\n114\t- Use realistic terminology relevant to your application domain\n115\t\n116\t### Defining the input schema\n117\t\n118\tThe `inputSchema` follows [JSON Schema](https://json-schema.org/) format. The model uses this to construct the correct input.\n119\t\n120\t- Use `required` to mark mandatory fields\n121\t- Add `description` to each property -- the model reads these\n122\t- Tool parameter names use `snake_case` (this is the convention from the AI provider API, wrap them in `/* eslint-disable camelcase */` comments)\n123\t\n124\t### Writing the executor\n125\t\n126\tA `ToolExecutor` is an async function that takes the tool input and returns either a string or a `ToolResponse`:\n127\t\n128\t<!-- doc-block: src/orchestration/tools/registry.ts#ToolExecutor -->\n129\t```typescript\n130\ttype ToolExecutor = (input: Record<string, unknown>, context?: ToolContext) => Promise<string | ToolResponse>;\n131\t```\n132\t\n133\tThe optional `context` provides `userId`, `sessionId`, `workspaceId`, and `authHeaders` for tools that need to make authenticated API calls.\n134\t\n135\t- Return `JSON.stringify(result)` for most tools -- the result gets added to the conversation as a tool result message\n136\t- Cast input fields from `unknown` to their expected types\n137\t- Handle missing or unknown input gracefully (return a reasonable default or error message)\n138\t\n139\tFor tools that need to send messages directly to the client or suppress the AI's echo, return a `ToolResponse` object instead of a plain string. See [tool-responses.md](../specs/hal-engine-tool-responses/spec.md) for a full walkthrough.\n140\t\n141\t## Step 2: Register the tool\n142\t\n143\tOpen `src/orchestration/tools/index.ts` and add two lines:\n144\t\n145\t<!-- doc-block: example/register-tool.ts#register -->\n146\t```typescript\n147\timport {weatherTool, executeWeather} from './weather-tool.js';\n148\t\n149\t// ... existing registrations ...\n150\t\n151\ttoolRegistry.register(weatherTool, executeWeather);\n152\t```\n153\t\n154\tThat is it. The `ToolRegistry` feeds all registered tool definitions to the chat orchestrator, which passes them to the AI provider. {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"call_d52041e1476e47f3bd28e103","type":"tool_result","content":"# Adding a New Tool\n\nTools let the AI model fetch data or perform actions during a conversation. When the model decides it needs information (like weather data or a database lookup), it invokes a tool by name, the server executes it, and the result feeds back into the conversation.\n\nAdding a new tool takes two steps: define it and register it. The rest is automatic -- the orchestrator passes tools to the AI provider, and the client already knows how to render any tool entry.\n\n## Step 1: Create the tool file\n\nCreate a new file in `src/orchestration/tools/`. Each tool exports two things:\n\n- A **`ToolDefinition`** describing the tool's name, purpose, and input schema\n- A **`ToolExecutor`** function that runs the tool and returns a JSON string\n\nHere is a complete example:\n\n<!-- doc-block: example/weather-tool.ts#weather-tool -->\n```typescript\nimport type {ToolDefinition, ToolExecutor} from '@re-cinq/hal-engine';\n\nexport const weatherTool: ToolDefinition = {\n  name: 'get_weather',\n  description:\n    'Get the current weather for a location.\\n\\n' +\n    'Use this tool when the user:\\n' +\n    '* Asks about weather or temperature\\n' +\n    '* Wants to know conditions at a specific place\\n' +\n    '* Needs a forecast for planning\\n\\n' +\n    'Returns temperature, conditions, humidity, and wind speed.',\n  promptInstructions:\n    'Use this when users ask about weather at a specific location. {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"call_23b700bf2ab5453b9d48d283","type":"tool_result","content":"1\tname: CI\n2\t\n3\ton:\n4\t  pull_request:\n5\t  push:\n6\t    branches: [main]\n7\t  # Manual runs: re-checking a branch against a moved main, or confirming a gate after\n8\t  # changing one, without pushing an empty commit.\n9\t  workflow_dispatch:\n10\t  # An advisory published after a merge is invisible until someone opens a pull request, and this\n11\t  # repository can go days without one. Monday 07:00 UTC; only `build-chain` answers it.\n12\t  schedule:\n13\t    - cron: '0 7 * * 1'\n14\t\n15\t# Every job here only reads the checkout; the repo default is write.\n16\tpermissions:\n17\t  contents: read\n18\t\n19\t# A newer push to the same branch supersedes an in-flight run. main is exempt:\n20\t# every commit there should have its own recorded result.\n21\tconcurrency:\n22\t  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}\n23\t  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.ref != 'refs/heads/main' }}\n24\t\n25\tjobs:\n26\t  verify:\n27\t    name: Verify\n28\t    # The scheduled run exists for the dependency audit; re-running the suite on an unchanged\n29\t    # tree every Monday would report nothing new.\n30\t    if: github.event_name != 'schedule'\n31\t    runs-on: ubuntu-latest\n32\t    steps:\n33\t      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1\n34\t        with:\n35\t          persist-credentials: false\n36\t          # Full history, not for this job but for the spec anchor check below:\n37\t          # it resolves cited content from\n38\t          # origin/main, which a shallow clone cannot serve.\n39\t          fetch-depth: 0\n40\t\n41\t      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0\n42\t        with:\n43\t          node-version: '22'\n44\t          cache: npm\n45\t\n46\t      # --ignore-scripts so `prepare` does not build on install: what a lifecycle script\n47\t      # runs is out of this workflow's control, and the Build step below is where a broken\n48\t      # compile should be reported. Type check catches it earlier still.\n49\t      - name: Install\n50\t        run: npm ci --ignore-scripts\n51\t\n52\t      # Every `npm run` step below is one link of the `verify` script in\n53\t      # package.json, in the same order - scripts/verify-script.test.ts holds\n54\t      # the two together - and kept as separate steps so a red run names the\n55\t      # gate that failed rather than a single opaque command.\n56\t      - name: Type check\n57\t        run: npm run typecheck\n58\t\n59\t      # example/ is outside tsconfig.json's rootDir, so nothing checked the one\n60\t      # file the README and the guide are written against.\n61\t      - name: Type check the example\n62\t        run: npm run typecheck:example\n63\t\n64\t      - name: Lint (--max-warnings 0)\n65\t        run: npm run eslint\n66\t\n67\t      # Reports, never blocks. The one rule it runs is `warn`, so the step exits\n68\t      # 0 on its own and carries no continue-on-error: a non-zero exit here now\n69\t      # means the config itself broke, and that should fail. Its findings render\n70\t      # as warning annotations rather than failures, which is what a report on a\n71\t      # passing check should look like.\n72\t      #\n73\t      # require-statement-links counts spec statements with no test behind them.\n74\t      # Most of what it reports needs a test written rather than a line changed,\n75\t      # so the count is meant to be visible on every run and to fall over time.\n76\t      # Its test-side mirror, require-spec-link, is satisfied and gates in the\n77\t      # Lint step above. Never add a rule here to escape a red gate -\n78\t      # eslint.config.backlog.mjs says what belongs.\n79\t      - name: Spec traceability backlog (report)\n80\t        run: npm run lint:backlog\n81\t\n82\t      - name: Format check\n83\t        run: npm run prettier:check\n84\t\n85\t      # Runs the whole suite and fails it on the committed coverage floor in\n86\t      # jest.config.js, so this is the test gate rather than an extra pass.\n87\t      - name: Test (with coverage floor)\n88\t        run: npm run test:coverage\n89\t\n90\t      - name: Build\n91\t        run: npm run build\n92\t\n93\t      # Anchors drift silently: a cited file gaining or losing lines above the\n94\t      # cited one leaves the link pointing at different content, and the spec\n95\t      # still reads as cited. Resolves content at origin/main, which the\n96\t      # fetch-depth: 0 above exists to provide. A red check is fixed by running\n97\t      # `node scripts/repoint-spec-anchors.mjs` and committing the result.\n98\t      - name: Spec anchor check\n99\t        run: node scripts/repoint-spec-anchors.mjs --check origin/main\n100\t\n101\t      # A citation counts as coverage only in its statement's trailing\n102\t      # parenthetical; one written mid-statement is dropped by the Lore job in silence,\n103\t      # so the spec reads as cited while its coverage is zero. A red check is\n104\t      # fixed by moving the link to the end of its statement, never by deleting\n105\t      # it (AGENTS.md § Spec Test Links).\n106\t      # Every fenced typescript block in the three documented files is generated\n107\t      # from source; hand transcription is what produced the defects this catches.\n108\t      - name: Documented code blocks\n109\t        run: npm run docs:check\n110\t\n111\t      # Three rules that held only because somebody remembered them: a path in prose that resolves,\n112\t      # a spike that says it is a spike, and an example region inside the EU.\n113\t      - name: Documented paths resolve\n114\t        run: npm run docs:check-paths\n115\t\n116\t      - name: Spike documents carry a status block\n117\t        run: npm run docs:check-spikes\n118\t\n119\t      - name: Documented regions\n120\t        run: npm run check:regions\n121\t\n122\t      # A line number is a derived pointer; the name is what the author cited. This catches a citation\n123\t      # whose line moved under it, which no baseline comparison can see on a branch that edits the spec.\n124\t      - name: Spec citations name their test\n125\t        run: npm run spec:names\n126\t\n127\t      - name: Spec link placement\n128\t        run: npm run check:spec-links\n129\t\n130\t      # Lead paragraphs and a spec's status-vs-coverage are ESLint's job; the\n131\t      # one verdict a `files` glob cannot express - that an ADR's frontmatter\n132\t      # status parses, without holding the ADR to the coverage tier - is this\n133\t      # script's. `check:spec-status -- --coverage` lists unlinked statements\n134\t      # and never gates.\n135\t      - name: Spec status\n136\t        run: npm run check:spec-status\n137\t\n138\t      # A release note and a commit subject have different readers, so this is a\n139\t      # file the author writes rather than something derived from the log. It needs the tree installed but nothing built, so it\n152\t  # skips `prepare` with --ignore-scripts.\n153\t  build-chain:\n154\t    name: Build chain\n155\t    runs-on: ubuntu-latest\n156\t    steps:\n157\t      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1\n158\t        with:\n159\t          persist-credentials: false\n160\t\n161\t      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0\n162\t        with:\n163\t          node-version: '22'\n164\t          cache: npm\n165\t\n166\t      - name: Install (no build)\n167\t        run: npm ci --ignore-scripts\n168\t\n169\t      # Full tree, dev included: those packages are what a runner installs\n170\t      # before building dist/, and the release workflow signs what it produces.\n171\t      - name: Audit (high and above)\n172\t        run: npm run check:audit\n173\t\n174\t      # A tag is a mutable pointer its owner can repoint under a job that holds\n175\t      # repository credentials.\n176\t      - name: Action pins\n177\t        run: npm run check:action-pins\n178\t\n179\t  # Its own job because it is the only check that exercises the package as a\n180\t  # consumer receives it - packed, installed outside this tree, with no optional\n181\t  # peer present. Everything else here tests the source in place, where every\n182\t  # dependency is already installed and every one of these failures is invisible.\n183\t  smoke:\n184\t    name: Smoke (packed tarball)\n185\t    if: github.event_name != 'schedule'\n186\t    runs-on: ubuntu-latest\n187\t    steps:\n188\t      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1\n189\t        with:\n190\t          persist-credentials: false\n191\t\n192\t      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0\n193\t        with:\n194\t          node-version: '22'\n195\t          cache: npm\n196\t\n197\t      - name: Install (no build)\n198\t        run: npm ci --ignore-scripts\n199\t\n200\t      # Explicit, rather than relying on `npm pack` to trigger `prepare`: a build failure should be\n201\t      # reported by a step named Build, not as a confusing pack error inside the smoke script.\n202\t      - name: Build\n203\t        run: npm run build\n204\t\n205\t      # Two variants, two jobs' worth of signal in one: `bare` is a mock-provider consumer with no\n206\t      # optional peer, `full` is a Bedrock or Vertex consumer with both. They fail differently and\n207\t      # separate steps name which consumer is broken.\n208\t      - name: Smoke (no optional peer)\n209\t        run: npm run smoke -- bare\n210\t\n211\t      - name: Smoke (both optional peers)\n212\t        run: npm run smoke -- full\n213\t"}]},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"ee11d90f-fc8e-4737-93f5-aee635892159","uuid":"eb669700-7fa2-4244-8bab-2a374a2f4baa","timestamp":"2026-11-03T11:11:30.456Z","tool_use_result":{"type":"text","file":{"filePath":"/var/tmp/loop-bench/runs/ed7c55279f96/workspace/target/.github/workflows/ci.yml","content":"name: CI\n\non:\n  pull_request:\n  push:\n    branches: [main]\n  # Manual runs: re-checking a branch against a moved main, or confirming a gate after\n  # changing one, without pushing an empty commit.\n  workflow_dispatch:\n  # An advisory published after a merge is invisible until someone opens a pull request, and this\n  # repository can go days without one. Resolves content at origin/main, which the\n      # fetch-depth: 0 above exists to provide. A red check is fixed by running\n      # `node scripts/repoint-spec-anchors.mjs` and committing the result.\n      - name: Spec anchor check\n        run: node scripts/repoint-spec-anchors.mjs --check origin/main\n\n      # A citation counts as coverage only in its statement's trailing\n      # parenthetical; one written mid-statement is dropped by the Lore job in silence,\n      # so the spec reads as cited while its coverage is zero. A red check is\n      # fixed by moving the link to the end of its statement, never by deleting\n      # it (AGENTS.md § Spec Test Links).\n      # Every fenced typescript block in the three documented files is generated\n      # from source; hand transcription is what produced the defects this catches.\n      - name: Documented code blocks\n        run: npm run docs:check\n\n      # Three rules that held only because somebody remembered them: a path in prose that resolves,\n      # a spike that says it is a spike, and an example region inside the EU.\n      - name: Documented paths resolve\n        run: npm run docs:check-paths\n\n      - name: Spike documents carry a status block\n        run: npm run docs:check-spikes\n\n      - name: Documented regions\n        run: npm run check:regions\n\n      # A line number is a derived pointer; the name is what the author cited. {"type":"assistant","message":{"id":"msg_202611031916241f511711ca5c46af","type":"message","role":"assistant","model":"glm-5.3-flash","content":[{"type":"tool_use","id":"call_e31d09bff9384785ab7e86d0","name":"Write","input":{"file_path":"/var/tmp/loop-bench/runs/ed7c55279f96/workspace/target/src/orchestration/tools/registry.ts","content":"import Ajv from 'ajv';\nimport type {ErrorObject, ValidateFunction} from 'ajv';\nimport type {ToolDefinition} from '../../types/ai.js';\nimport type {OutgoingMessage} from '../../types/messages.js';\nimport {log} from '../../shared/logger.js';\n\nexport interface ToolResponse {\n  result: string;\n  clientMessages?: OutgoingMessage[];\n  suppressAssistantResponse?: boolean;\n}\n\nexport interface ToolContext {\n  userId: string | number;\n  sessionId?: string;\n  workspaceId?: string | number;\n  authHeaders?: {\n    cookie?: string;\n    authorization?: string;\n    host?: string;\n  };\n}\n\nexport type ToolExecutor = (input: Record<string, unknown>, context?: ToolContext) => Promise<string | ToolResponse>;\n\nexport function normalizeToolResponse(response: string | ToolResponse): ToolResponse {\n  return typeof response === 'string' ? {result: response} : response;\n}\n\nexport type ToolDefinitionSource = ToolDefinition | (() => ToolDefinition);\n\nexport interface RegisteredTool {\n  definition: ToolDefinition;\n  execute: ToolExecutor;\n}\n\ninterface StoredTool {\n  definitionSource: ToolDefinitionSource;\n  execute: ToolExecutor;\n  staticValidator?: ValidateFunction;\n}\n\nexport class ToolRegistry {\n  private readonly tools = new Map<string, StoredTool>();\n  private readonly validatorsBySchema = new WeakMap<object, ValidateFunction>();\n\n  private resolveDefinition(source: ToolDefinitionSource): ToolDefinition {\n    return typeof source === 'function' ? source() : source;\n  }\n\n  private validatorFor(toolName: string, schema: Record<string, unknown>): ValidateFunction {\n    const cached = this.validatorsBySchema.get(schema);\n    if (cached) return cached;\n    const compiled = compileSchema(toolName, schema);\n    this.validatorsBySchema.set(schema, compiled);\n    return compiled;\n  }\n\n  register(definition: ToolDefinitionSource, execute: ToolExecutor): void {\n    const resolved = this.resolveDefinition(definition);\n    const staticValidator =\n      typeof definition === 'function' ? undefined : compileSchema(resolved.name, resolved.inputSchema);\n    this.tools.set(resolved.name, {definitionSource: definition, execute, staticValidator});\n  }\n\n  get(name: string): RegisteredTool | undefined {\n    const tool = this.tools.get(name);\n    if (!tool) return undefined;\n    return {definition: this.resolveDefinition(tool.definitionSource), execute: tool.execute};\n  }\n\n  getDefinitions(): ToolDefinition[] {\n    return [...this.tools.values()].map(t => this.resolveDefinition(t.definitionSource));\n  }\n\n  getPromptInstructions(): string[] {\n    return this.getDefinitions()\n      .filter(t => t.promptInstructions)\n      .map(t => `${t.name}: ${t.promptInstructions}`);\n  }\n\n  getExamplePrompts(): string[] {\n    return this.getDefinitions().flatMap(t => t.examplePrompts ?? []);\n  }\n\n  has(name: string): boolean {\n    return this.tools.has(name);\n  }\n\n  /** Validates input against the registered inputSchema and returns a rejection ToolResponse instead of throwing — see specs/hal-engine-tool-input-validation/spec.md. */\n  async execute(name: string, input: Record<string, unknown>, context?: ToolContext): Promise<ToolResponse> {\n    const tool = this.tools.get(name);\n    if (!tool) {\n      log.warn('tool', 'tool not found', {name});\n      throw new Error(`Unknown tool: ${name}`);\n    }\n    const resolved = this.resolveDefinition(tool.definitionSource);\n    const validator = tool.staticValidator ?? this.validatorFor(resolved.name, resolved.inputSchema);\n    if (!validator(input)) {\n      const failures = (validator.errors ?? []).map(error => describeFailure(error));\n      log.warn('tool', 'input rejected', {name, failures});\n      return {result: `${resolved.name} rejected the input: ${failures.join('; ')}`};\n    }\n    log.info('tool', 'executing', {name, inputKeys: Object.keys(input)});\n    const rawResult = await tool.execute(input, context);\n    const response = normalizeToolResponse(rawResult);\n    log.info('tool', 'execution complete', {\n      name,\n      rawType: typeof rawResult,\n      clientMessageCount: response.clientMessages?.length ?? 0,\n      clientMessageTypes: response.clientMessages?.map(m => m.type) ??
